name: readme-check

# Fails when README.md / README_EN.md drift out of sync with the repo:
# a *-cli/ directory nobody mentions, or a stated CLI count that is stale.
#
# Run it locally with the same script the workflow uses:
#   ./scripts/check-readme.sh

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*-cli/**'
      - 'README.md'
      - 'README_EN.md'
      - 'scripts/check-readme.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/readme-check.yml'

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./scripts/check-readme.sh

## Contributing a new recipe

Write a new markdown file mirroring the structure of an existing recipe and open a PR. Each should include:

- **When to use**: what real need would lead someone here
- **Setup**: which CLIs to install, which sites to log into
- **Send to Claude**: the copy-paste prompt (code-fenced)

- **Uses**: CLI and skill links

# 调研「2025 本地 AI 模型」话题

[English](./research-local-ai-models_EN.md) | 中文

## 场景

要快速摸清一个不熟悉的话题——比如想看看 2025 年的本地 AI 模型生态怎么样了。手动一篇篇 Google 读过来太慢，让 AI 跑搜索、抓正文、整理结论。

## 前置

- [kimi-webbridge](https://www.kimi.com/zh-cn/features/webbridge)
- 从 [Releases](https://github.com/better-world-ai/x-cli/releases) 下载并安装 google-cli 或 baidu-cli

## 发给 Claude

```
帮我搜 "best local AI models 2025"，把 Google 前 10 个结果的正文都抓回来。
然后做两件事：
1. 用 200 字左右总结这些文章的共识观点和分歧点
2. 列一张表，整理这些文章提到的所有模型，按推荐次数排序

中文输出，原始链接附在最后。
```

## 你会拿到

- 一段精炼的综合摘要（共识 + 分歧）
- 一张模型对比表（名称、推荐它的文章数、主要优势、典型用例）
- 原始结果链接列表，方便点进去看细节
- 如果某些页面抓取失败（付费墙、403），AI 会标注跳过

## 用到

[google-cli](../google-cli/) 或 [baidu-cli](../baidu-cli/)

## 改一改

- **中文话题**：用 baidu-cli 替代 google-cli
- **调整数量**：前 5 个还是前 20 个都行
- **加约束**：只看近 30 天的、排除特定网站、按时间排序
- **换输出形式**：摘要、对比表、SWOT、问答 FAQ、PPT 大纲都能直接说

# Research the "2025 local AI models" topic

English | [中文](./research-local-ai-models.md)

## When to use

You need to get up to speed on an unfamiliar topic fast — say, what the local AI model landscape looks like in 2025. Reading article after article by hand is slow. Let the AI run the search, pull the bodies, and consolidate.

## Setup

- [kimi-webbridge](https://www.kimi.com/features/webbridge)
- Download google-cli or baidu-cli from [Releases](https://github.com/better-world-ai/x-cli/releases)

## Send to Claude

```
Search "best local AI models 2025" and fetch the body text of the top 10 Google results.
Then do two things:
1. Summarize the consensus points and disagreements in about 200 words
2. List every model mentioned across these articles in a table, sorted by recommendation count

Output in English, with the original links at the end.
```

## What you'll get

- A tight consolidated summary (consensus + disagreements)
- A model comparison table (name, number of articles recommending it, key strengths, typical use cases)
- The original result links so you can drill in
- If any pages fail to scrape (paywall, 403), the AI flags which ones were skipped

## Uses

[google-cli](../google-cli/) or [baidu-cli](../baidu-cli/)

## Adapt

- **Chinese topics**: swap google-cli for baidu-cli
- **Result count**: top 5 or top 20, your call
- **Constraints**: last 30 days only, exclude certain domains, sort by date
- **Output format**: summary, comparison table, SWOT, Q&A FAQ, or slide outline — just ask

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps README.md / README_EN.md honest about what the repo actually contains.
#
# Two things drifted before and prompted this check:
#   - boss-cli and scholar-cli were added but never mentioned in either README
#   - both READMEs claimed "12 CLIs" long after the count reached 14
#
# Portable to macOS bash 3.2 / BSD find as well as CI.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

fail=0
note() { printf '  x %s\n' "$1"; fail=1; }

clis=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '*-cli' | sed 's|^\./||' | sort)
count=$(printf '%s\n' "$clis" | grep -c .)
echo "found $count CLI directories"

# 1. every CLI directory is mentioned in both READMEs
for readme in README.md README_EN.md; do
  for cli in $clis; do
    grep -qF "$cli" "$readme" || note "$readme never mentions $cli"
  done
done

# 2. the stated count matches reality.
# If you reword these sentences, update the patterns here too.
check_claim() { # <file> <regex matching the number in context> <label>
  hits=$(grep -oE "$2" "$1" || true)
  if [ -z "$hits" ]; then
    note "$1: no '$3' sentence found - reworded? update scripts/check-readme.sh"
    return
  fi
  for n in $(printf '%s\n' "$hits" | grep -oE '[0-9]+'); do
    [ "$n" = "$count" ] || note "$1 says $n where the repo has $count ($3)"
  done
}

check_claim README.md    '[0-9]+ 个 CLI'      "N 个 CLI"
check_claim README.md    '这 [0-9]+ 个'        "这 N 个"
check_claim README_EN.md 'All [0-9]+ CLIs'    "All N CLIs"
check_claim README_EN.md 'All [0-9]+ in this' "All N in this repo"

if [ "$fail" = 0 ]; then echo "README is in sync"; else echo "README is out of sync with the repo"; fi
exit "$fail"

name: release

# Per-CLI release. Tag a specific subdir to release just that CLI:
#   git tag baidu-cli/v0.1.0         && git push --tags
#   git tag google-cli/v1.0.0        && git push --tags
#   git tag nanobanana-cli/v0.2.0    && git push --tags
#   git tag chatgpt-image-cli/v1.3.0 && git push --tags
#
# Manual trigger from the Actions tab is also supported (for ad-hoc builds).

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'baidu-cli/v*'
      - 'google-cli/v*'
      - 'nanobanana-cli/v*'
      - 'chatgpt-image-cli/v*'
      - '58-cli/v*'
      - 'anjuke-cli/v*'
      - 'apartments-cli/v*'
      - 'rightmove-cli/v*'
      - 'idealista-cli/v*'
      - 'gaokao-cli/v*'
      - 'booking-cli/v*'
      - 'ctrip-cli/v*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      cli:
        description: 'Which CLI to build'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
          - baidu-cli
          - google-cli
          - nanobanana-cli
          - chatgpt-image-cli
          - 58-cli
          - anjuke-cli
          - apartments-cli
          - rightmove-cli
          - idealista-cli
          - gaokao-cli
          - booking-cli
          - ctrip-cli
      version:
        description: 'Version label (e.g. v0.0.0-test). Used in release name only.'
        required: true
        default: 'v0.0.0-manual'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: prepare ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_name || format('{0}/{1}', inputs.cli, inputs.version) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      cli: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.cli }}
      version: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.tag }}
      manual: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.manual }}
    steps:
      - id: parse
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
            CLI="${{ inputs.cli }}"
            VERSION="${{ inputs.version }}"
            TAG="${CLI}/${VERSION}-${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
            MANUAL=true
          else
            REF="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}"   # e.g. google-cli/v1.0.0
            CLI="${REF%%/*}"                 # google-cli
            VERSION="${REF#*/}"              # v1.0.0
            TAG="$REF"
            MANUAL=false
          fi
          echo "cli=$CLI" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "manual=$MANUAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Resolved -> cli=$CLI version=$VERSION tag=$TAG manual=$MANUAL"

  build:
    name: build ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }} ${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
    needs: prepare
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - goos: darwin
            goarch: arm64
            ext: ''
            archive: tar.gz
          - goos: darwin
            goarch: amd64
            ext: ''
            archive: tar.gz
          - goos: linux
            goarch: amd64
            ext: ''
            archive: tar.gz
          - goos: linux
            goarch: arm64
            ext: ''
            archive: tar.gz
          - goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            ext: '.exe'
            archive: zip
          - goos: windows
            goarch: arm64
            ext: '.exe'
            archive: zip
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}/go.mod
          cache: true
          cache-dependency-path: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}/go.sum

      - name: build
        working-directory: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}
        env:
          CLI: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
          CGO_ENABLED: '0'
          EXT: ${{ matrix.ext }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Build the binary with the bare CLI name (so users get e.g. `google-cli`
          # after extraction, not `google-cli-darwin-arm64`).
          bin="${CLI}${EXT}"
          go build -trimpath \
            -ldflags="-s -w -X main.version=${VERSION}" \
            -o "$bin" .
          ls -la "$bin"
          file "$bin" || true

      - name: package archive
        working-directory: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}
        env:
          CLI: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}
          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
          EXT: ${{ matrix.ext }}
          ARCHIVE: ${{ matrix.archive }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bin="${CLI}${EXT}"
          stem="${CLI}-${GOOS}-${GOARCH}"
          if [[ "$ARCHIVE" == "tar.gz" ]]; then
            tar -czf "${stem}.tar.gz" "$bin"
            ls -la "${stem}.tar.gz"
          else
            zip -q "${stem}.zip" "$bin"
            ls -la "${stem}.zip"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}/${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.${{ matrix.archive }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  release:
    name: publish ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
          merge-multiple: true
          pattern: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-*

      - name: checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: |
          sha256sum * > checksums.txt
          ls -la

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
          name: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }} ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
          target_commitish: ${{ github.sha }}
          prerelease: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.manual == 'true' }}
          files: dist/*
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          generate_release_notes: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.manual == 'false' }}
          body: |
            Release of `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}` ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}.

            ## Downloads

            | Platform | Asset |
            |---|---|
            | macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon) | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` |
            | macOS amd64 (Intel)         | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-darwin-amd64.tar.gz` |
            | Linux amd64                 | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-linux-amd64.tar.gz` |
            | Linux arm64                 | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |
            | Windows amd64               | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-windows-amd64.zip` |
            | Windows arm64               | `${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-windows-arm64.zip` |

            Checksums: `checksums.txt` (sha256).

            ## Install (macOS arm64 example)

            ```bash
            curl -LO https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}/${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
            tar -xzf ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
            ./${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }} --help
            ```

            Linux / other archs: swap the suffix (`linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`, etc.). Windows: download the `.zip` and extract.

            > **macOS users**: browser-downloaded archives get blocked by Gatekeeper. After extracting, clear the quarantine flag once:
            > ```bash
            > xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}
            > ```

            See [README](https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/tree/main/${{ needs.prepare.outputs.cli }}#readme) for usage.
